answers.why: Judah is judged alongside all the inhabitants of Jerusalem for their idolatry.
The God of Israel defends his people against Moab and Ammon.
Israel has a remnant described with plural verbs and pronouns.
Israel is commanded to shout alongside Zion and Jerusalem.
Zerubbabel is governor of Judah, the province and its people.
Judah is the community governed by Zerubbabel as the people rebuild the temple.
Zerubbabel governs Judah and is addressed alongside the remnant of the people.
Judah names the province governed by Zerubbabel.
The horns scattered Israel alongside Judah and Jerusalem.
The LORD inherits Judah as his portion in the holy land alongside restored Jerusalem.
The Philistine remnant becomes like a governor within Judah's community.
Chariots are removed from Ephraim's territory in parallel with horses from Jerusalem.
Judah is pictured as God's bow in the conflict of Zion's sons against Greece's sons.
Ephraim fills God's bow as part of the forces raised against Greece.
